justification: Adds a third build-blocking ratchet and opens a defect row covering 16% of every served provision. It serves no number to a user, so not Critical — but a cap seeded wrong would either block all work or enforce nothing, and the new row changes what the ledger claims about the corpus.

falsifiable_check.command: python scripts/dq_check.py && python scripts/dq_probe_live.py --id DQ-68 && python -m pytest tests/test_dq_check.py -q
falsifiable_check.fails_when: dq_check exits 1 the moment a row is declared fixed while carrying no check and the count passes 46 — so a defect can no longer be closed on a memory. DQ-68 exits 1 while any served provision lacks a topic. test_the_fixed_cap_matches_reality fails if the cap is left above the real count, and test_the_three_ratchets_measure_different_sets fails if any of the three caps quietly becomes an alias for another.
falsifiable_check.observed_red: Observed live. Marking DQ-58 fixed without writing a probe — the exact case this exists to stop — produced 'DQ-CHECK: FAILED - a row was declared FIXED with nothing to prove it. fixed rows with no check: 47, cap is 46' and exit 1; restoring the file returned exit 0. DQ-68's probe exits 1 printing 3,197 with its query. The trial run also exposed a flaw in my own failure message: slicing the sorted list at the cap and calling the tail 'the new row' named DQ-9, which had nothing to do with the change, so the message now says plainly that it counts and cannot identify which row is new, and points at git diff instead.

pre_impl.existing_data: regulatory_provisions (19,957 served rows) for DQ-68's count. .claude/dq_checks.json for the caps. Read-only — no database writes.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: Assumes 'fixed with no check' is worth freezing rather than driving to zero. Zero would require a probe written against 46 already-closed defects; a target nobody can meet gets deleted rather than met, which is the failure mode the older _max_no_check cap of 57 already demonstrates. Freezing stops the case still worth stopping — a NEW row closed on a memory.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: The cap is seeded at today's real count (46), so nothing currently green turns red. DQ-68 is a new row that arrives already red, which is the honest state for a defect nobody was watching.
pre_impl.external_source_error: N/A — no network. The probe reads the database through the shared read-only helper, which exits 2 (UNKNOWN) rather than clean when it cannot connect.
pre_impl.user_failure_mode: None user-facing. For a developer: closing a defect without a probe now fails the build and explains why 'fixed' with nothing behind it is a claim about the past.

functions.name: _no_check_cap
functions.input: a key naming which of the three caps to read from .claude/dq_checks.json
functions.output: the integer ceiling for that count, or None when the key is absent or not a plain int, in which case that ratchet is skipped rather than treated as zero
functions.if_none: The ratchet does not run. A missing cap must not block every build, and bool is rejected explicitly because bool subclasses int and a stray `true` would otherwise ratchet at 1.

functions.name: run
functions.input: a DQ id, looked up in the PROBES table where the new DQ-68 entry supplies its SQL and the prose explaining a non-zero count
functions.output: an exit code plus the count printed WITH the query that produced it, so the row's status is generated by running rather than retyped — 0 only when the count is 0
functions.if_none: An unknown id is reported rather than treated as clean; an unreachable database exits 2 so 'could not measure' is never rendered as 'nothing wrong'.

values.nullable: yes — absent means the ratchet does not run
values.guard_at: tests/test_dq_check.py::test_the_fixed_cap_matches_reality asserts it exists AND equals the live count
values.if_missing: Without the test a missing or inflated cap would silently disable the rule — the 'check nobody invokes' failure this repo has hit three times.

values.value: fixed_no_check — the list of fixed rows with no check
values.if_missing: An empty list would mean every fixed row can prove itself; today it is 46 and the failure message no longer pretends to know which one is new.

queries.purpose: DQ-68: served provisions across every document carrying no topic
queries.where_clause: is_current AND v2_is_actionable AND v2_topic IS NULL
queries.if_zero: The row is declared open, so 0 makes the ledger ratchet go RED — correct, it would mean tagging is complete and the status is stale.
queries.if_wrong: Dropping v2_is_actionable would count rows nobody is served and inflate the figure well past the real exposure. Keeping the same scope as DQ-24 is deliberate: it makes DQ-24 a strict subset, so the two numbers are comparable rather than two different measures of the same thing.

break_it.scenario: Someone closes an open defect as fixed without writing a probe for it.
break_it.what_happens: The ledger records a fix that nothing can verify, and a regression is invisible — DQ-54 sat declared FIXED while still broken.
break_it.how: scripts/dq_check.py:585 fails the build once the count passes 46. Verified live by marking DQ-58 fixed: exit 1 at 47 against cap 46.
break_it.repro: Set any open row's declared to 'fixed' without adding a check, then run python scripts/dq_check.py

break_it.scenario: The failure message names an innocent row, sending someone to fix the wrong thing.
break_it.what_happens: Time is spent on a row that was never the problem, and trust in the check drops.
break_it.how: The original slice-the-tail approach did exactly this in a trial run, naming DQ-9. The message now states that it counts and cannot identify which row is new, and points at `git diff origin/main -- .claude/dq_checks.json`.
break_it.repro: Mark any row fixed without a check and read the output

break_it.scenario: The cap is raised, or left high after a check is written, so the ratchet becomes a rubber stamp.
break_it.what_happens: Slack accumulates and the next unproven closure gets in free.
break_it.how: test_the_fixed_cap_matches_reality asserts cap == live count, so both raising it and forgetting to lower it fail CI. Same discipline as the other two caps.
break_it.repro: Set _max_fixed_without_check to 99 and run python -m pytest tests/test_dq_check.py -q

break_it.scenario: Two of the three caps quietly start measuring the same set, so one of them enforces nothing.
break_it.what_happens: A ratchet that looks live but duplicates another — three numbers, two meanings, and nobody notices which one stopped mattering.
break_it.how: test_the_three_ratchets_measure_different_sets pins all three against their live counts and asserts the unresolved and fixed sets are disjoint and together no larger than the total.

break_it.scenario: DQ-68 duplicates DQ-24 so the same rows are counted by two open defects and one is closed on the other's progress.
break_it.what_happens: Tagging the Transport SEPP would appear to close both, leaving 2,674 rows untracked again.
break_it.how: Both use the identical served-set scope, so DQ-24 is a strict SUBSET of DQ-68 (523 of 3,197) rather than an overlapping measure. Both rows state that relationship and the residual, so closing DQ-24 visibly leaves DQ-68 at 2,674.
break_it.repro: python scripts/dq_probe_live.py --id DQ-24 and --id DQ-68; the first count is contained in the second

break_it.scenario: DQ-68's query is mis-scoped — it drops is_current or v2_is_actionable, or the topic column holds an empty string rather than NULL.
break_it.what_happens: The count measures something other than the served exposure. Too wide and it reports a defect against rows nobody sees, so the row gets dismissed as noise; too narrow, or blind to empty-string topics, and it reads clean while provisions still reach reports untagged.
break_it.how: Scope was measured before the row was written, not assumed: 3,197 of 19,957 served rows (16.0%), against 1,248 further non-actionable untagged rows for the Transport SEPP alone that are deliberately excluded. The breakdown by council was checked too (statewide 2,530, marrickville 475, leichhardt 123), so the number has a shape a reader can sanity-check rather than a bare total. The scope is stated in the probe's own means text, which prints with every run alongside the query.
break_it.repro: python scripts/dq_probe_live.py --id DQ-68 prints the count WITH its query; re-run without the v2_is_actionable filter to see the number move and confirm which rows the change admits.
